chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim, from 'Ali, from Abi Basir, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who places his hand on the body of his wife while he is fasting.
So he said: There is no harm, and if madhy is emitted, it does not break the fast.
He said: And His saying, “Do not have direct contact with them,” means intercourse during the daytime in the month of Ramadan.

key_terms.صَائِمٌ: one who is observing the fast
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or legal objection
key_terms.لَا تُبَاشِرُوهُنَّ: do not have direct intimate contact with them

ai.seo_question: Does touching one's wife or emitting madhy break the fast in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about physical contact between a fasting man and his wife. It states that touching her body does not invalidate the fast, and even if madhy is emitted, the fast is not broken. It also explains the prohibition of direct sexual approach in Ramadan daytime as referring to intercourse.
